main_text.p: αὐτὸς γράφων; deinde, ὃν τὰ βαθύτερα τῶν νοη-μάτων αὐτοῖς ἐπιστέλλει; tandem, quod scribat κατηχουμένοις [?] τὰ ὑψηλά. Et has ipsas putamus esse causas, discrepantiæ illius omnis in Epistola ad Hebræos. 1. Quod Paulus majore jam studio & accuratiore iisdem scripserit. Ut sublimi illo eloquio, sapientiæ sublimitatem suæ, hominibus iniquiùs de se sentientibus, inter cætera exponeret. 11. Quod Epistolæ argumentum ferè diversum à reliquis esset. Magis etiam arduum ac sublime, ubi de Christi persona supra Angelos, suprà Mosem, suprà creaturas omnes evecta; ubi abstrusissima redemptionis nostræ mysteria, collata jam cum illis figurarum umbrarumque involucris: ubi historia Christi in cœlis agentis, sacerdotio æterno defungentis, solio majestatis insidentis, è cœlo opitulantis, suos Patri æterno sacrificio propitiantis &c. Qui sanè Paulus quasi intra velum consistebat, altissima cœlorum penetrabat, omnem illum terrestris sacerdotij, & sanctuarij mundani, & Mosaici cultus quantumvis splendidum deprime-

page.notes: The Greek line at the head is partly unclear in the scan. "κατηχουμένοις" and the following word were read with difficulty; the word after "κατηχουμένοις" is marked [?]. Check the Greek against the original. The line-end break "νοη-μάτων" is copied with the hyphen as it appears; the hyphen itself is faint. The page number "174" is blotted; the [?] marks it as doubtful. "11." is copied as printed (possibly intended as "II."). The running head is read as "Epistola" with the final letter hidden by print damage.
